_meta.ruling: SHA approved the Marma x Sacred Tones placement map, proposal v2, 2026-09-10.
_meta.source: Vasant Lad and Anisha Durve, Marma Points of Ayurveda: The Energy Pathways for Healing Body, Mind and Consciousness, The Ayurvedic Press. Locations, doshic subtypes, vitality classes and traditional associations are drawn from the region chapters and from chapters 2, 3 and 8.
_meta.scope: 27 of the tradition's 117 points. Every point here earns its place by matching a Sacred Tones fork's own bone application point or a chakra centre. The set is deliberately small.
_meta.excluded: The genital and perineal points of the classical set (Bhaga, Medhra, Yoni Jihva, Vrushana, Yoni Oshtha, Guda) are excluded from Astryx entirely and must never be added. See applicationType fieldOnly and the reproductive zone rule in BodyPlacementEngine.

applicationTypes.weighted: A weighted fork stem may rest on the point with steady, comfortable contact.
applicationTypes.field: Light contact at most, or the fork held in the field. Never deep pressure.
applicationTypes.fieldOnly: Never contacted at any pressure. The fork is held six inches out and swept.

_meta.anchorSpace: x and y are fractions of the body image, matching bodyMapAnchorLibrary in BodyPlacementEngine.ts. Paired points carry xLeft and xRight.
_meta.tierSeam: Individual tier renders sanskrit, english, plainLocation, applicationType and safetyNote. The practitioner tier adds location, doshicSubtypes, element, vitalityClass, anatomicalRelation and contraindications. Enforced in sacredShape.ts.
_meta.lineage: Vasant Lad and Anisha Durve, Marma Points of Ayurveda (The Ayurvedic Press) - locations, doshic subtypes, vitality classes and traditional associations

points.plainLocation: The very top of the head.
points.location: On the vertex at the midline, ten anguli back from the midpoint between the eyebrows. Found by drawing a line from the apex of each ear to where they meet at the top of the skull.
points.vitalityLabel: One of the Eight Great points
points.anatomicalRelation: Associated in the source with the subarachnoid space and cerebrospinal fluid, the middle cerebral artery, the mid-cranial fossa, and the hypothalamic-pituitary axis.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Regulating prana and bringing prana and apana into step
Cerebral and cerebrospinal fluid circulation
Memory, attention and concentration
Settling the mind and steadying the emotions
points.name_note: Adhi means first or origin and pati means master. The source calls it the first master of all the points.
points.safetyNote: One of the Eight Great points. Light, steady contact only. Never percussive force, and never on an infant or a child whose fontanelles have not closed.

points.plainLocation: Just behind the top of the head.
points.location: On the midline, two anguli behind Adhipati and twelve anguli back from the midpoint between the eyebrows.
points.vitalityLabel: One of the Eight Great points
points.anatomicalRelation: Associated with the posterior cerebral artery, the posterior cranial fossa, the cerebellum and the third ventricle.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Regulating tarpaka kapha
Occipital and parietal ease
Cerebrospinal fluid circulation
Recall and positive memory
points.name_note: Translated as the opening to Shiva. It sits at the top of the sushumna alongside Adhipati.
points.safetyNote: One of the Eight Great points, and the source asks for gentle stimulation here. Hold the fork in the field or use featherlight contact only.

points.plainLocation: The centre of the forehead, just above the point between the eyebrows.
points.location: On the midline of the forehead, one angula above the glabella.
points.vitalityLabel: One of the Eight Great points
points.anatomicalRelation: Associated with the hypothalamus, the optic chiasm and the frontal lobe, and described as the bridge between the pineal and pituitary glands.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Steadying the fluctuations of the mind
Hormonal balance through the pineal and pituitary bridge
Concentration and insight
Releasing held stress
points.name_note: Ajna means order. Sthapani means establishment or steadiness.
points.safetyNote: One of the Eight Great points and close to the eyes. Gentle, steady contact on the frontal bone only. Never let the fork stem slide toward the eye socket.

points.plainLocation: The soft hollow at each temple.
points.location: At the temple, in the depression one to two anguli behind the outer end of the eyebrow.
points.vitalityLabel: Classed by the source as an extremely vital point
points.anatomicalRelation: Associated with the temporal lobe, the mid-cranial fossa and the temporalis muscle.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Strongly settling pitta
Ease in the temples
Cooling heat held in the upper body
Softening intense or fiery emotion
points.name_note: Shankha means conch. The temporal bone resembles part of a conch shell.
points.safetyNote: The source is explicit that heavy pressure must be avoided here, and the point sits close to the eye. Hold the fork in the field. Never press the stem into the temple.
contraindications: Active migraine with aura, unless they ask for it

points.plainLocation: The hollow at the base of the skull, where the head meets the neck.
points.location: In the depression immediately below the occipital protuberance.
points.anatomicalRelation: Associated with the posterior cranial fossa, the posterior cerebral artery, the occipital bone and the hypothalamus.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Cerebral and cerebrospinal fluid circulation
Lymphatic flow at the base of the skull
Neck ease and range of motion
Balance and equilibrium
Kindling agni in the stomach and pancreas
points.name_note: Mula means root and manya means neck. The beginning of the neck.
points.safetyNote: Steady, comfortable contact on the bony ridge. Stop if the person feels dizzy or light-headed.

points.plainLocation: Either side of the spine at the very top of the neck.
points.location: On the back of the neck, level with the lower border of the spinous process of C1, one angula out from the midline on each side.
points.vitalityLabel: Classed by the source as a vital point
points.anatomicalRelation: Level with the first cervical vertebra and the upper intraspinal nerves. The source relates the right side to the liver and the left to the spleen.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Anchoring and steadying the mind
Ease in the neck and the back of the head
Regulating rakta dhatu, the blood tissue
The eyes
points.name_note: From the root dhru, to hold. Literally that which holds the skull, and also that which holds consciousness.
points.safetyNote: A delicate region. Light, steady contact only, with the head supported and the neck neutral. Never apply force or leverage here.
contraindications: Any history of spinal cord involvement

points.plainLocation: Either side of the spine at the top of the neck, one finger below Vidhuram.
points.location: On the back of the neck, level with the lower border of the spinous process of C2, one angula out from the midline on each side, directly below Vidhuram.
points.vitalityLabel: Classed by the source as a delicate point
points.anatomicalRelation: Level with the axis vertebra. Associated with the hypothalamus, the medulla oblongata, the intraspinal nerves and the upper lobes of the lungs.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Ease in the neck, head and ears
Releasing tension, stress and held emotion
Opening the breath in the upper lungs
Loosening the weight carried across the shoulders
points.name_note: Krikatika means axis, the joint that lets the skull rotate. It also carries the sense of responsibility.
points.safetyNote: The source names this a delicate area. Light, steady contact only, head supported, neck neutral. Never apply force or leverage here.
contraindications: Any history of spinal cord involvement

points.plainLocation: The front of the throat, in the soft hollow just above the hyoid bone.
points.location: On the anterior midline of the neck, in the depression above the hyoid bone.
points.vitalityLabel: Classed by the source as an extra vital point
points.anatomicalRelation: Associated with the thyroid and parathyroid, the vocal cords and larynx, the pharynx and trachea.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Regulating udana vayu, the upward-moving breath
Voice and speech
Opening the airway and calming the breath
Releasing what has gone unsaid
points.name_note: Kantha means throat. The source ties it directly to Vishuddhi, the throat centre, whose name means purity.
points.safetyNote: The source states that every point of the throat is very sensitive and requires gentle pressure. Astryx holds the fork in the field here. Never press on the front of the throat.
contraindications: Any pressure on the front of the throat

points.plainLocation: The flat of the upper breastbone, just below the notch at the base of the throat.
points.location: On the midline of the manubrium sterni, slightly below the suprasternal notch.
points.vitalityLabel: Delicate. The source asks for a light touch.
points.anatomicalRelation: Sits in front of the thymus, which the source calls ojo granthi, the seat of ojas. Associated with the trachea and bronchi, the cardiac and tracheal plexuses and the thyroid.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Immunity and the building of ojas
Kindling dhatu agni and clearing ama
Steady respiration
Lymphatic flow in the chest
Devotion, and the meeting of the inner world with the outer
points.name_note: Jatru means to preserve or maintain. The source describes tapping it lightly several times to wake the immune response, which is precisely what a struck fork stem does.
points.safetyNote: A delicate point over the breastbone. Light, steady contact only. Never percussive force.
contraindications: A pacemaker or implanted cardiac device

points.plainLocation: The centre of the breastbone, level with the third space between the ribs.
points.location: On the anterior midline at the level of the third intercostal space.
points.vitalityLabel: One of the Eight Great points
points.anatomicalRelation: Associated with the right side of the heart and the pericardium, and with the oesophagus, trachea and bronchi.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Steady cardiac rhythm and coronary circulation
Open airways
Settling the mind and balancing the emotions
Releasing prana held stagnant in the chest
points.name_note: Hrid means heart. The source notes that a tulsi or rudraksha mala worn so it touches this point helps the heart centre find its balance.
points.safetyNote: One of the Eight Great points, directly over the heart. Astryx holds the fork in the field here. Never place a vibrating stem over the heart.
contraindications: A pacemaker or implanted cardiac device
Recent cardiac event or chest surgery

points.plainLocation: The top of each shoulder, on the ridge of muscle halfway between the neck and the point of the shoulder.
points.location: At the superior aspect of the trapezius, midway between the tip of the spinous process of C7 and the tip of the acromion.
points.anatomicalRelation: Overlies the brachial gateway at C7 and the trapezius. The source relates the right side to the liver and the left to the spleen.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Ease and range in the shoulder
Carrying prana into the lungs and upper chest
Occipital tension that rises from the shoulders
Releasing stagnant, unexpressed feeling
points.name_note: Skandha carries the sense of shouldering responsibility. The source links it to the weight people carry across the shoulders.
points.safetyNote: Comfortable contact on the muscle ridge. Ease off if the arm tingles or goes numb.
contraindications: Pregnancy, where this point is traditionally avoided

points.plainLocation: Just below the bottom tip of each shoulder blade.
points.location: Immediately below the inferior angle of the scapula on both sides.
points.anatomicalRelation: The source relates the right side to the liver and gallbladder and the left to the heart and spleen.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Diaphragmatic expansion and easy breathing
Steady prana vayu through the breath
Ease across the scapula and between the ribs
Circulation through the liver and the spleen
points.name_note: From bru, to increase or expand. Bruhati also means support.
points.safetyNote: Comfortable contact over muscle and rib, never over the spine itself.

points.plainLocation: On the right side, where the lower edge of the ribs crosses a line dropped from the middle of the collarbone.
points.location: Where a vertical line from the mid-clavicular point meets the costal margin on the right side of the body.
points.anatomicalRelation: Associated with the liver and gallbladder, and with the head of the pancreas, the right kidney, the hepatic flexure and the right adrenal.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Liver and gallbladder function
Kindling bhuta agni, the metabolic fire of the liver
Digestion and the metabolism of the seven tissues
Settling fiery emotion
points.name_note: Ya means circulation and krut means action. Yakrut is simply the liver.
points.safetyNote: Comfortable contact on the rib margin. Ease off over soft abdomen. Stop at any tenderness.
contraindications: Acute abdominal pain of any kind

points.plainLocation: On the midline of the belly, halfway between the navel and the bottom tip of the breastbone.
points.location: On the midline of the abdomen, at the midpoint between the umbilicus and the tip of the xiphoid process.
points.anatomicalRelation: Associated with the stomach and pancreas and with the celiac region.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Kindling jathara agni, the digestive fire
Steady digestion and appetite
Settling pitta and the heat it carries
Harmonising the emotions held in the belly
points.name_note: The full name is Surya Mandala. Surya is the sun and mandala is a vortex. The source calls it the microcosmic sun within us.
points.safetyNote: Comfortable contact on the soft belly, never deep pressure. Work only on an empty or light stomach.

points.plainLocation: The centre of the navel.
points.location: At the centre of the umbilicus.
points.vitalityLabel: One of the Eight Great points
points.anatomicalRelation: Associated with the small intestine, the mesenteric lymph nodes, the omentum and the abdominal aorta.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: The seat of samana vayu and the root of the nadis
Digestion and absorption
Building ojas and carrying it through the tissues
Grounding the breath into the belly
points.name_note: Nabhi means the centre, and also the place with no fear. The source names it the central pole that harmonises the crown and the sole.
points.safetyNote: One of the Eight Great points and directly over the abdominal aorta. Astryx holds the fork in the field here rather than pressing.
contraindications: Hernia at or near the navel

points.plainLocation: On the midline below the navel, in the lower belly.
points.location: At the midpoint of a line drawn from the umbilicus toward the upper border of the pubic bone.
points.vitalityLabel: Classed by the source as an extra vital point
points.anatomicalRelation: Associated with the bladder and the pelvic organs.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Regulating apana vayu, the downward-moving breath
Bladder tone and the water channels
Circulation through the pelvic bowl
points.name_note: Basti means bladder. The source calls it the premier point for regulating apana vayu.
points.safetyNote: Never contacted. This point sits inside the reproductive and pelvic-floor zone, so the fork is held six inches out and swept. That rule holds for every fork, every chart and every person.
contraindications: Contact of any kind, at any pressure
Pregnancy, where the sweep widens further

points.plainLocation: Either side of the spine at the small of the back, just above the sacrum.
points.location: One angula lateral to the lower border of the spinous process of L5, on each side.
points.anatomicalRelation: Level with the fifth lumbar vertebra at the lumbosacral hinge.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Ease across the low back
Stability through the lumbosacral hinge
Regulating apana vayu
points.name_note: Worked alongside Kati, which sits just below it on the sacrum.
points.safetyNote: Comfortable contact over bone and muscle beside the spine, never on the spinous process itself. Person prone and clothed.

points.plainLocation: On the flat plate of the sacrum, in the first pair of small hollows below the small of the back.
points.location: In the first posterior sacral foramen, on each side.
points.anatomicalRelation: Associated with the sacroiliac joint and, through apana vayu, with the pelvic organs and the colon.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Stability through the sacroiliac joint and the lumbopelvic girdle
Regulating apana vayu
Ease across the low back
Posture and locomotion
points.name_note: Kati means hip or waist. It is the place a wrapped cloth touches.
points.safetyNote: Worked over the bony plate of the sacrum with the person prone and clothed. This is the sacral doorway in Astryx. Comfortable contact only, never over the coccyx or below it.
contraindications: Pregnancy, where this resolves to a field sweep

points.plainLocation: The very base of the spine, at the tail bone.
points.location: At the tip of the coccyx.
points.anatomicalRelation: At the sacral angle and the triangular tip of the coccyx.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Grounding, and the base of the spine
Regulating apana vayu
The pelvic floor
The seat of dormant kundalini, which the source describes rising from here to the crown
points.name_note: Trik means triangle, for the sacral angle. The source states plainly that Trik stimulates energy at Muladhara and Adhipati at Sahasrara, the two ends of one channel.
points.safetyNote: Never contacted. This point sits inside the field-only zone, so the fork is held six inches out and swept downward. That rule holds for every fork, every chart and every person.
contraindications: Contact of any kind, at any pressure

points.plainLocation: The bony tip of each elbow.
points.location: On the elbow, at the tip of the olecranon process of the ulna.
points.vitalityLabel: An asthi marma, a bone point
points.anatomicalRelation: Directly on the olecranon. The source classes it an asthi marma because it lies on bone.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Coordination and range through the elbow and forearm
Shleshaka kapha, which lubricates the joints
Local ease at the elbow
points.name_note: Kurpara means corner, for its place at the bend of the arm. The source names it a bone point, which makes it the natural home for the Saturn fork.
points.safetyNote: Comfortable contact on the bony tip. Avoid the ulnar groove on the inner side, where the nerve runs close to the surface. Ease off at any tingling into the hand.

points.plainLocation: On the inside of each forearm, two fingers below the crease of the elbow.
points.location: Two anguli below the midpoint of the cubital crease.
points.anatomicalRelation: Over the upper forearm between the ulna and radius, close to the median and ulnar pathways.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Steadying the mind and holding focus
Colon function, which Ayurveda calls the seat of vata
Kindling agni and clearing ama
Releasing stagnant feeling
points.name_note: Indrabasta means the stable crown of Indra. The source ties it to steadiness and persistence, which is why Astryx pairs it with Uranus.
points.safetyNote: Comfortable contact on the muscle of the forearm. Ease off at any tingling into the hand.

points.plainLocation: The centre of each palm, where the middle finger touches when the hand makes a fist.
points.location: On the palm, in the depression between the second and third metacarpals.
points.anatomicalRelation: Associated with the heart through vyana vayu, the diaphragm through udana vayu and the lungs through prana vayu.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Settling the mind and steadying the emotions
Releasing held stress
The lungs and the diaphragm
Grounding an overactive current
points.name_note: The heart or centre of the palm. The source calls it the solar plexus of the hand, since the hand is a small map of the whole chakra system.
points.safetyNote: Comfortable contact in the centre of the palm. A very safe and well-tolerated point.

points.english: The power of the thighs, front
points.plainLocation: The middle of the front of each thigh, on the big muscle.
points.location: At the level of the mid thigh on the anterior surface of the quadriceps.
points.anatomicalRelation: Over the femoral shaft and the quadriceps. The source relates the right thigh to the ascending colon and the left to the descending colon.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Circulation through the lower limbs
Strength and upward-moving energy through udana vayu
The kidneys and bladder
Steadying vata-type shifting discomfort
points.name_note: Sakthi urvi means the power or energy of the thighs.
points.safetyNote: Comfortable contact on the muscle of the thigh. Keep well clear of the inner thigh and the groin.
contraindications: Any known blood clot in the leg

points.plainLocation: The centre of each kneecap.
points.location: At the centre of the patella.
points.anatomicalRelation: Directly on the patella and the knee joint capsule.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Ease and stability through the knee
Shleshaka kapha, which lubricates the joint
Circulation through the lower limbs
Settling inflammatory heat held in the joint
points.name_note: Janu simply means knee. Bone, joint and lubrication together, which is the Saturn signature.
points.safetyNote: Comfortable contact on the kneecap. Ease off at any sharp pain in the joint.
contraindications: Recent knee surgery or joint replacement
Any blood clot in the leg

points.plainLocation: The middle of the fullest part of each calf.
points.location: In the centre of the belly of the gastrocnemius, on the line connecting posterior Janu to Parshni.
points.anatomicalRelation: Over the calf muscle along the tibial line. The source relates the right leg to the ascending colon and the left to the descending colon.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Circulation through the lower limbs
Releasing cramp and holding in the calf
Colon function and the vata emotions Ayurveda seats there
Steadying the mind
points.name_note: Basta means colon. Indrabasta is described as the inner door of the colon.
points.safetyNote: Comfortable contact on the calf muscle. Do not work this point if there is any calf tenderness, swelling or warmth, which needs a doctor first.
contraindications: Any suspected blood clot, which is an urgent medical matter

points.plainLocation: The back of each heel, just below the heel bone.
points.location: One angula below the calcaneal tubercle on the posterior aspect of the heel.
points.anatomicalRelation: On the calcaneus, at the head of the posterior chain that runs up the back of the leg.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Bringing prana and apana into balance in the pelvic bowl
Circulation through the feet
Ease along the back of the leg
Grounding
points.name_note: Parshni means heel. Astryx uses it as the Earth Day fork's primary point because it reaches the root of the body without approaching it.
points.safetyNote: Comfortable contact on the heel bone. A very safe and well-tolerated point.
contraindications: Reduced sensation in the feet, where less pressure is needed

points.plainLocation: The centre of the sole of each foot, about a third of the way down from the base of the second toe.
points.location: On the sole between the second and third metatarsals, one third of the distance along a line from the base of the second toe to the heel.
points.anatomicalRelation: Associated in the source with the pancreas and the diaphragm.
traditionallyAssociatedWith: Bringing excess energy down out of the head
Grounding and equilibrium
Settling the mind before rest
Ease through the feet and lower limbs
points.name_note: Pada is foot and madhya is middle. The source pairs it with Adhipati at the crown to balance the body's polarity, with Nabhi as the pole between them.
points.safetyNote: Comfortable contact on the sole. A very safe and well-tolerated point, and the standard close for a session.
contraindications: Reduced sensation in the feet, where less pressure is needed
